selection_rule: Two bounded questions per existing reference entry; quote and locate the actual entry assertion before testing it. A question is not a presumption that the entry or historical claim is true. If the exact proposed link is not asserted, record that limit rather than invent an entry claim.

questions.question: Check the entry's evidence for Sumerian/Akkadian language contact and the separation of scribal language survival from spoken-language replacement; which dated text or scholarly passage supports the institutional coupling?
Check its kaunakes or tufted/skirt-dress terminology against a dated object or scholarly source; distinguish modern/Greek descriptive naming, pictured texture and actual fibre/garment construction.

Check the entry's rn/name-efficacy or mdw-ntr language/divinity link against an identifiable text or scholarly passage; do not make every receipt a spell or treat an English gloss as a complete theology.

Check one explicit linen/pleating or garment-status claim using a dated material object or technical source; separate artistic convention, surviving textile and a complete cutting/pleating reconstruction.

Verify the entry's distinction between undeciphered Linear A/Minoan affiliation and readable Greek Linear B: sign similarity and B-based transliteration are not proof of Minoan pronunciation, meaning or divine names.

Check the relationship and limits between Linear B textile accounts and elite painted/figurine costume: does an actual cited tablet/object/scholarly passage support the claimed material or institutional link without a one-to-one garment identification?
Check the entry's Hittite/Hattic/Luwian/Hurrian language-versus-ritual layering against a located text or scholarly passage; separate script, language affiliation and a deity's cult provenance.

Check one dated divine/royal headgear, pointed-cap or horned-crown identification in the entry; distinguish depicted rank, deity/king identification and earlier Hattic or later Neo-Hittite comparators.
Check the entry's oracle-bone language, divination and royal-ancestor coupling using an inscription/corpus or scholarly passage; do not turn one archive's genre into all Shang speech or belief.
Check one bronze/jade, dressed-rank or ritual-vessel terminology claim and its period: separate Shang object evidence, Zhou institutions and later transmitted ritual prescriptions.
Check mlqrt/Melqart's king-of-the-city analysis and the limits of a fixed merchant-patron/theological profile against an inscription, philological source or scholarly passage.

Check the entry's purple-dye production/elite display coupling using actual archaeological or technical evidence; distinguish a dye workshop/object from a universal king-only wearing law and native garment term.

Check the entry's divine-name writing/reading/register distinction against a located textual or scholarly source; retain textual-date and transmission limits, not a recovered universal ancient pronunciation.

Check priestly garment terminology and the evidential status of the cited biblical prescription; distinguish a dated transmitted text and its translation from excavated dress or a uniform for all Israelites.

Check Old Persian/Elamite/Babylonian royal trilingualism and its administrative limits using an inscription or archive passage; distinguish monumental ideology from the languages of all subjects and daily provisioning.

Check the winged-figure/Faravahar identification problem against scholarly wording: separate contemporary caption, proposed Ahuramazda/fravashi/xvarenah identification and modern ethical feather/ring diagrams.

Check the entry's Etruscan language/alphabet relationship using epigraphic or scholarly evidence; readable adapted Greek letters do not establish Indo-European affiliation or complete lexical understanding.

Check the Liber Linteus textile-text object biography and ritual-calendar interpretation against a museum/research source; distinguish original writing/use, later Egyptian mummy reuse, date and garment inference.

Check the entry's use of later Kiche Popol Vuh as a controlled comparison for Classic Maya myth and language; locate the manuscript/translation/era mediation rather than treating it as a Classic inscription.

Check one named jade regalia/divine-embodiment or royal costume claim using a dated object, inscription or scholarly passage; separate object provenance and visible form from an exact ancient semantic or wearer identification.

Check the entry's Meroitic decipherment-versus-understanding and proposed language-family affiliation distinction using a scholarly passage; sound values are not unrestricted translation or identity with Old Nubian.

Check kandake/title translation and royal-woman identification against a text/object or scholarly passage; keep reigning queen, queen mother, royal imagery and universal gender-system claims separate.

Check the located Gobhila naming-rule claim (2.8.8-17) or the entry's shiksha six-concern passage against the named school/edition: distinguish textual rule, translator's terminology and universal ancient practice.

Check the Satapatha consecration black-antelope skin/horn or cloth passage: distinguish sitting surfaces versus worn garment and school-specific prescription versus a pan-Vedic costume reconstruction.
